topic: Coldest national capital: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia — the only capital with a sub-zero annual mean (≈ −0.4 to −1.3 °C depending on period); Astana second; altitude ~1,350 m; January nights below −30 °C; ~1.6 million people, about half of Mongolia's ~3.5 million
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Ottawa or Moscow is the coldest capital.
myths.reality: Ulaanbaatar is the only national capital whose annual mean temperature is below 0 °C; Astana is second; Ottawa and Moscow both average several degrees above freezing.

worldatlas_cold.title: The Coldest Capital Cities In The World
worldatlas_cold.notes: Ulaanbaatar annual mean −0.8 °C, the only capital with a sub-zero average, at over 1,300 m; Astana second (4.2 °C)

wiki_ub.title: Ulaanbaatar
wiki_ub.notes: coldest national capital; elevation ~1,350 m; climate box (NOAA normals) annual mean below 0 °C, January mean around −21 °C with nightly lows below −30 °C; population ≈ 1.6–1.7 million, about half of Mongolia

noaa_normals.title: WMO Climate Normals 1991–2020 — Ulaanbaatar (44292)
noaa_normals.notes: station normals for Ulaanbaatar: annual mean temperature below 0 °C; January mean minimum below −25 °C; station elevation ≈ 1,300 m

nso_mongolia.title: Population of Mongolia / Ulaanbaatar
nso_mongolia.notes: Mongolia ≈ 3.5 million (2024); Ulaanbaatar ≈ 1.7 million — about half the national population

britannica_ub.title: Ulaanbaatar
britannica_ub.notes: capital of Mongolia on the Tuul River at about 1,350 m; extreme continental climate; largest city with roughly half the population

wiki_astana.title: Astana
wiki_astana.notes: second-coldest national capital after Ulaanbaatar; annual mean ≈ 3.5–4 °C

claims.text: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, is the coldest national capital and the only one whose annual mean temperature is below 0 °C.
vo: where is the coldest capital city on earth
mongolia. ulaanbaatar is the only capital on earth whose average temperature, over the whole year, is below freezing

claims.text: January nights in Ulaanbaatar fall below −30 °C; Astana, Kazakhstan, is the second-coldest capital; Ottawa's annual mean is around 6–7 °C.
vo: january nights there pass minus 30. astana, in kazakhstan, is second; ottawa is not close

claims.text: Ulaanbaatar sits at about 1,350 m above sea level on a continental plateau far from any ocean, which drives its extreme climate.
vo: the secret is height: the city sits over 1,300 metres up, on a plateau far from any ocean

claims.text: About half of Mongolia's ~3.5 million people live in Ulaanbaatar (≈ 1.6–1.7 million).
vo: and about half of all mongolians live in it, more than 1,600,000 people in a single cold valley
